title: 120 new Kero experiment candidates
selection: 120 independently authored experiment designs and substantive controlled extensions informed by the supplied 147-case catalogue and the pinned Kero source. Not a list of 120 demonstrated working runs.

reference.review_method: Web review of the supplied catalogue and relevant pinned source files. The complete baseline JSON was not ingested locally for automated semantic or bytewise deduplication.

run_instructions.procedure: Write one experiment script verbatim to experiment.lab and run it in its own fresh CLI process. Do not concatenate scripts or reuse a populated bench.
run_instructions.note: The wrapper JSON is a dataset container; pass an extracted .lab script to kero run, not this JSON. Start with a small selected group and inspect model refusals and the acceptance criteria.

scope: All 120 entries are designed_not_run. observed_result and validated_on are null; no output, binary hash, commit validation, or chemistry pass has been invented.
Native command spellings and the four named organic transformations follow the pinned source. A custom offline subset linter was run, not the official Rust parser or the Kero engine.
Registered input identity is not proof that every desired reaction, solid, complex or physical-property model is supported. High-risk routes are identified per entry.
These are new experimental questions or substantive controlled extensions, not 120 new chemical reaction families. The collection includes physical chemistry, analyses and separations.
Importance and educational stages are editorial estimates. They do not establish mandatory coverage in any individual German state curriculum.
Designed for simulation only. These scripts are not wet-lab directions, school safety assessments, chemical purchasing advice, or permission to mix hazardous substances.

Within-file IDs, full-script hashes and comment-stripped script bodies are unique. Exhaustive comparison against the original catalogue was not performed locally; the provided validator accepts a local --baseline file.
A successful process exit is never sufficient to label a case chemically correct. Compare saved observations with each acceptance criterion and retain unsupported/inconclusive outcomes.

experiments.title: Conductometric strong-acid titration: a minimum, not only an endpoint
experiments.script:
# AB-001: Conductometric strong-acid titration: a minimum, not only an endpoint
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 HCl 0.001mol
measure v1 conductivity
measure v1 ph
add v1 NaOH 0.0005mol
measure v1 conductivity
add v1 NaOH 0.0005mol
measure v1 conductivity
measure v1 ph
add v1 NaOH 0.0005mol
measure v1 conductivity
measure v1 ph
inspect
experiments.expected_result: Conductivity falls as highly mobile hydrogen ions are replaced by sodium ions, reaches a minimum near equivalence, and rises with excess hydroxide.

expected_processes.interpretation: Educational chemical equation, not an assertion that the runtime implements every species or pathway.

acceptance_checks.criterion: The equivalence snapshot has lower conductivity than both the initial acid and final excess-base snapshots.
pH crosses from acidic to near-neutral to alkaline; conductivity does not become zero.

novelty.basis: New design or substantive controlled extension relative to the supplied catalogue; not a claim of a novel discovery.
novelty.distinction: Adds a conductivity-versus-stoichiometry trajectory to the existing endpoint neutralisations.

limitations: Compare hydrogen-ion activities rather than treating all solutions as ideal; solution volume and neutral pH can change with temperature.
